what: R9, the light loop's key-collision rule, measured on the TRAINED checkpoint. Two prompts sharing a prefix up to the read token give identical keys in a causal model; an edit set containing such a pair would have its crowding inflated by its own construction. Checked on the KEYS, not the prefix strings, because collinearity is a fact about what the model does with the prompt.
finding: clean at every size: the worst pair rises with n (0.642 at n=8 to 0.894 at n=256) but never approaches collinearity, and zero pairs exceed 0.95 anywhere. So the n=256 crowding figure of 0.9385 is geometry, not duplicated keys.
contrast: on an UNTRAINED net of the same architecture the same construction gives a worst pair of 0.9995 with all 24 prefixes distinct - so the prefix-level form of the rule is insufficient, and that is what the plant in retrain.py asserts.
not_verified: this is one seed's case construction per size. It says the sets actually used here are clean; it does not bound what another seed or another position sampler would produce, which is why the check is a standing plant rather than a one-off clearance.
